item.title: Serbia’s Student List vows to halt arms trade with Israel, signalling a break with Vucic
item.description:
Serbia’s Student List vows to halt arms trade with Israel, signalling a break with Vucic

Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Tue, 11/17/2026 - 13:57
Critics say arms sales to Israel served former president's interests. Ending the trade could prove harder than pledging to do so
MPs from Serbia's Student List meet supporters of the student-led movement in front of the National Assembly in Belgrade on 17 November 2026, as the newly elected parliament prepares to hold its inaugural session (AFP)
Off

Serbia’s election-winning Student List has pledged to halt arms trade with Israel and called for an end to an Israeli-linked drone project in Serbia, signalling a potential break with the close military ties that former President Aleksandar Vucic cultivated.

Filip Ubovic, a Student List representative, announced the pledge last week on a podcast hosted by British journalist Aaron Bastani.

“What is happening there is a stain on humanity’s conscience, and it is truly regrettable. Our platform clearly states that we will end the arms trade with Israel,” said Ubovic when asked about Israel’s war on Gaza.

The Student List won 140 of 250 seats in the 25 October snap election, securing an outright majority and defeating Vucic’s bloc after years of accusations of growing authoritarianism and corruption under his rule.

In September, a month before the election, Vucic inaugurated a factory assembling Israeli-made drones in Serbia.

Serbian arms exports to Israel rose from $1.5m to $45.8m in 2024, according to a joint investigation by the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network and Haaretz. The surge coincided with Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

Serbia also stepped up its purchases of Israeli weapons. In early 2025, it bought Elbit Systems’ PULS artillery systems and Hermes drones for $335m. In August that year, it bought long-range missiles, drones and electronic warfare equipment for about $1.6bn.

Elbit, the controversial Israeli arms manufacturer, has sought to expand in the Balkans in recent years, pursuing factory projects in Serbia and Albania.

'The issue is how to implement this break gradually without fully destroying the partnership with Israel, and without making Israel an enemy'

- Vuk Vuksanovic, King’s College 

How Elbit’s investments in Serbia and the country’s ties with Israel will develop “remains uncertain”, Vuk Vuksanovic, a lecturer in foreign policy and grand strategy at King’s College London’s Department of War Studies, told Middle East Eye.

“Serbian society has been historically divided on the Israeli-Palestinian issue, with some Serbs having emotional ties with the global Jewish community over the shared victimhood from World War II,” said Vuksanovic. “At the same time, many Serbs have expressed solidarity with Palestinians given the legacy of non-aligned Yugoslavia.

“In the past couple of years, especially with the rise of the Student Movement, we see increasing solidarity with Palestinians,” said Vuksanovic. He attributed the shift to growing global awareness of the plight of Palestinians.

“Many believe that the extent of the Gaza tragedy exceeds the past history of friendship with Israel and Israelis,” he added.

“For many Serbs, Vucic’s close ties with Israel, including ammunition deliveries, were not policies aimed at furthering Serbia’s national interest, but a self-interested move of the old clique to secure protection for Israel, its lobby groups, and, by extension, the Trump administration.” 

Vucic hits back

Vucic accused the Student List of weakening Serbia’s defences after Ubovic announced the pledge.

In a 12 November Instagram video, the former president portrayed the pledge as a refusal to cooperate with Israel. He also claimed the movement would refuse to work with China. Ubovic’s pledge concerned arms trade with Israel and the drone project in Serbia.

Israel’s embrace of Serb nationalist Milorad Dodik threatens Bosnia and the wider Balkans
Read More »

Vucic claimed that “the disintegration of the defence and security sector of Serbia has begun, and everything is on the order of foreign intelligence agencies”.

Vuksanovic warned that “while the desire and intention are noble and sincere, in practice this will be tougher to implement, as it has yet to be seen how to deprive the military industry of income, how to break technological and supply chain links set with the Elbit factory, and how firm the legal obligations stipulated in the contracts are.

“The issue is how to implement this break gradually without fully destroying the partnership with Israel, and without making Israel an enemy, and potentially its interest groups in the US,” he added.

“Paradoxically, this relationship may prove harder to transform than Serbia’s relations with the EU, the US, Russia, and China.” 

MEE contacted the Student List for comment and had received no response by the time of publication.

item.title: Crew abandon gas tanker off Hormuz after being hit by projectile, sources say
item.description:
Crew abandon gas tanker off Hormuz after being hit by projectile, sources say

The crew of a liquefied petroleum gas tanker abandoned ship on Tuesday after the vessel was struck by a projectile while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, maritime security sources said.

The crew of the Panama-flagged Tara Gas LPG tanker abandoned ship around 7 nautical miles (13 km) off Oman's Khasab coast, the sources said, and one crew member remains missing.

The vessel's Marshall Islands-based owner, listed in databases as Global Gas, could not be reached for comment.

The vessel last reported its position on September 26 off Oman's coast, according to ship tracking data on the MarineTraffic platform.

Earlier on Tuesday, British navy linked agency UKMTO said the crew of a tanker passing through the Strait of Hormuz was unaccounted for after it was attacked for a second time north of the port city of Khasab in Oman. It gave no further details.

Reporting by Reuters

item.title: Iraq orders Telegram block over national security and regulatory concerns
item.description: Iraqi authorities have ordered the blocking of the messaging application Telegram, citing national security concerns and the platform’s alleged failure to comply with legal and regulatory requirements. item.title: Israeli kills at least five in Gaza on Tuesday, including six-year-old
item.description:
Israeli kills at least five in Gaza on Tuesday, including six-year-old

At least four Palestinians, including a six-year-old boy, have been killed by Israeli forces so far today, medical sources cited in Reuters and Al Jazeera report.

According to medics cited by Reuters, two people, including six-year-old Eyas El-Nimnim, were killed in separate Israeli attacks in central Gaza's Deir el-Balah.

Meanwhile, another two were killed in attacks in the Khan Younis and Bir Al-Naja areas, in the south and north of the enclave.

Additionally, Al Jazeera reported earlier that a Palestinian man had succumbed to wounds sustained in an earlier Israeli strike on northern Gaza's Jabalia, while another person was severely wounded in an attack on Nuseirat refugee camp in Deir el-Balah.

item.title: Family of Palestinian journalist Mohammed Atiq demands his release
item.description:
Family of Palestinian journalist Mohammed Atiq demands his release

The family of Palestinian journalist Mohammed Atiq has demanded that his place of detention be disclosed and that he be released, following his arrest by the Israeli army at dawn on Sunday.

Israeli soldiers raided his home in the town of Burqin, west of Jenin, blew open the door, and searched the premises before taking Atiq to an unknown location. His family has yet to receive any information regarding his whereabouts or the conditions of his detention.

Atiq’s arrest comes amid an ongoing campaign of pursuit and detention targeting Palestinian journalists due to their professional work.

The Journalists' Syndicate has reported that approximately 210 journalists including about 23 women have been arrested since 7 October 2023. Meanwhile, the Palestinian Prisoners' Club confirms that 38 journalists, including five women, remain in Israeli occupation prisons.

Atiq works as a photojournalist for several international outlets, including Middle East Eye. About a month ago, he was detained for several hours while filming the olive harvest in the village of Anza, near Jenin.
